description: Upgrading from Kea 3.0.0 to 3.2.0 pulls in fixes for three high-severity (CVSS 7.5) remote denial-of-service vulnerabilities that were patched in the intervening 3.0.x point releases. All three allow an unauthenticated remote party to crash a Kea daemon; none permit code execution or data compromise. CVE-2025-40779 (fixed in 3.0.1) crashes kea-dhcp4 when a unicast client sends specific DHCPv4 options and Kea cannot find a matching subnet. CVE-2025-11232 (fixed in 3.0.2) crashes kea-dhcp4 via crafted hostname option content when default hostname-sanitization settings are combined with a non-empty ddns-qualifying-suffix. CVE-2026-3608 (fixed in 3.0.3) triggers a stack overflow in kea-ctrl-agent, kea-dhcp-ddns, kea-dhcp4, or kea-dhcp6 via deeply nested JSON sent to any API socket or HA listener; requiring mutual-TLS client certificates on those sockets mitigates it. Kea 3.2.0 itself carries no new CVE; it is a feature release (Control Agent removal, RADIUS/TLS, interface refactor) plus incidental hardening, including stricter config-file validation, tighter default file/package permissions, and a safer default for the HA listener's command restrictions.

URI 5.36 (released 2026-08-19) fixes a single security issue, CVE-2026-19953. The module's internal URI::_idna nameprep routine lowercased hostname labels but never applied Unicode Normalization Form C (NFC) before punycode encoding, even though RFC 5891 requires NFC normalization prior to IDNA A-label conversion. As a result, a hostname label that wasn't already in NFC could be encoded to a non-standard A-label that differs from — and doesn't round-trip to — the label a spec-compliant client would produce. For example, a precomposed Devanagari sequence encoded to xn--72b5c without normalization but to xn--11b2fg with it. This is a host-confusion vulnerability: code that extracts host() from a URI object built from untrusted input and uses it for security decisions (allow/deny lists, SSRF filters, cache keys, deduplication) could see a different host value than what an RFC-compliant HTTP client or resolver would actually contact — enabling filter bypass or SSRF. The fix applies proper NFC normalization in nameprep before A-label generation, aligning URI's host encoding with standard IDNA behavior.

WebKitGTK 2.52.6 addresses security issues from advisory WSA-2026-0005, covering nine CVEs. Most are memory-safety bugs in web content processing — including use-after-free issues (CVE-2026-64783, CVE-2026-64787), an out-of-bounds access (CVE-2026-64719), general memory corruption (CVE-2026-64757), and improved memory handling (CVE-2026-28984) — whose primary observed impact is an unexpected crash or process termination. The remaining fixes address policy and isolation bypasses rather than crashes: CVE-2026-43804 allowed a website visit to trigger an app denial-of-service; CVE-2026-64713 let sites detect whether a user had visited a given link; CVE-2026-64728 permitted malicious content to violate iframe sandboxing; and CVE-2026-64730 enabled UI spoofing from framed content. Each was fixed through improved memory handling, state management, bounds checking, or validation, as appropriate. Users are advised to upgrade to 2.52.6.

libheif 1.23.3, released September 1, 2026 as a dedicated security release, fixes ten security issues in the HEIF/AVIF decoder. The most severe is a critical heap buffer write overflow in the uncompressed (unci) mixed-interleave decoder (GHSA-x8r2-mgg j-j6wr), where a crafted file controls both the overflow length and the bytes written — the reason maintainers urged all users to upgrade. Three high-severity issues were also fixed: a decoder deadlock via an uncovered alpha-image reference cycle (GHSA-8fmq-r4p f-7m57), a heap out-of-bounds read leaking memory into decoded YCbCr-to-RGB output (GHSA-w7mc-p8j c-p853), and a buffer overflow plus double-free in the SVT-AV1 encoder plugin (GHSA-4jqm-2x3 4-6f6r). Five medium-severity fixes address further out-of-bounds reads and incomplete prior patches, including CVE-2026-84451 and CVE-2026-84450, plus null-pointer and allocation issues in example tools and bindings. One low-severity undefined-behavior fix rounds out the list. Most CVE identifiers were still pending assignment at release time.

libaom 3.15.0 (released August 25, 2026) addresses several security issues, with the release notes stating it "includes the fixes for all the security issues found by AI tools recently." The most significant is CVE-2026-56209 (CVSS 7.1, High), a bounds-check bypass in the SVC layer-ID control where a layer-count desync re-enabled out-of-bounds read/write access to encoder layer context structures; this release completes a previously incomplete fix for the issue, closing a path attackers could use for denial of service or potential code execution in network-facing encoders using SVC. A second flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-13906, addresses a potential heap out-of-bounds read in the motion estimation code caused by a stale stride value. Several additional memory-safety issues were fixed without CVE assignment: a heap double-free in multi-threaded encoding via aliased macroblock data, a heap buffer overflow in TXB context handling during SVC encoding with mismatched buffer sizes, a division-by-zero crash in the SVC encoder, a null-pointer/SEGV on failed encoder initialization, and undefined behavior from a NaN-to-integer conversion in noise model parameter handling. Most of these cluster around SVC encoding paths, suggesting concentrated fuzzing or review in that area this release cycle.

bubblewrap 0.12.0 (released August 26, 2026) fixes a symlink traversal vulnerability tracked as GHSA-pxhw- h44j-8pfx (a CVE has been requested but not yet assigned). During sandbox setup, bubblewrap could follow a symlink in attacker-controlled content that pointed back out to the host filesystem, causing files or directories intended for inside the sandbox to instead be created on the host — before the sandboxed process ever runs. This affects Flatpak and similar frameworks when processing a malicious or compromised app; created files are limited to the privileges of the user invoking bubblewrap, so the issue does not enable privilege escalation, but it does allow attacker-directed writes to arbitrary host paths reachable by that user. The fix uses openat2() with RESOLVE_IN_ROOT (with a fallback for systems lacking it) to correctly resolve absolute symlinks during setup. Notably, the fix could only be implemented in 0.12.0 and has no backport to older release branches, so upgrading is the only remediation. This release also removes support for building a setuid bubblewrap, since modern Linux distributions now generally support unprivileged user namespaces, further reducing historical attack surface.

libslirp 4.9.4 is a maintenance release; it does not introduce a dedicated security fix of its own, but it carries forward the fix for CVE-2026-9539, which was resolved upstream in v4.9.2 and remains present in 4.9.4. This issue was an out-of-bounds heap read and integer underflow in the TCP urgent-data handling routine (sosendoob() in src/socket.c). A privileged guest VM attacker (root or CAP_NET_RAW) could send crafted TCP segments with manipulated URG flags and urgent pointers to trigger the underflow, causing libslirp to read past the intended buffer and leak large amounts of host-process heap memory back to the guest. It was rated CVSS 3.1 6.5 (Medium) and fixed by capping the urgent-data count to what is actually available in the socket buffer, rather than trusting the guest-supplied urgent pointer. Versions 4.9.3 and 4.9.4 themselves are described by downstream packagers as minor releases with no new CVEs attributed to them. No other security-relevant changes were found documented for 4.9.4.

Dovecot 2.4.5 is a major security release, fixing roughly 18–22 CVEs according to downstream advisories. The issues span authentication bypass (including a trusted-network/proxy check that could be skipped via forged forwarded fields, and a SCRAM/CRAM channel-binding bypass allowing information disclosure), email spoofing caused by improperly handled SMTP message data, and several denial-of-service flaws — including excessive CPU or memory consumption from crafted Sieve contains matching, IMAP command bracing, NOOP parsing, and pre-authentication managesieve input. It also addresses an information leak in IMAP COMPRESS traffic, issues in OAuth2 authentication checks, and problems in dsync mailbox synchronization. Specific identifiers referenced by vendor advisories include CVE-2026-27852, CVE-2026-33263, CVE-2026-33604 through CVE-2026-33607, CVE-2026-40014, CVE-2026-40015, CVE-2026-40017, CVE-2026-40019, CVE-2026-42007, and CVE-2026-42391 through CVE-2026-42395, among others.

Exiv2 0.28.9, released August 30, 2026, fixes one moderate- and six low-severity vulnerabilities. The most notable is CVE-2026-68546, an out-of-bounds write in RemoteIo::Impl::populateBlocks(), triggered when Exiv2 reads metadata from a remote URL rather than a local file. Related low-severity issues in the same URL-handling code include an out-of-bounds read (CVE-2026-68547) and an out-of-bounds write in RemoteIo::mmap() (GHSA-vg6c-9f6h-4x5q< /a>). Other fixes address an out-of-bounds read in the CRW parser (CVE-2026-49275), an infinite-loop denial of service in QuickTimeVideo::userDataDecoder() triggered by crafted MOV files (GHSA-fgw8-p7pr-37cp< /a>), and excessive memory allocation in PgfImage::readMetadata() from crafted PGF files (GHSA-pwvq-9w4q-786w< /a>). The maintainers also announced plans to more systematically address recursive-parsing stack-exhaustion issues in the upcoming 0.29.0 release.

Net::DNS 1.57 fixes CVE-2026-81928, a memory-exhaustion denial-of-service caused by unbounded recursion in Net::DNS::RR::TSIG::sig_data(). When re-encoding a previously decoded message, sig_data strips TSIG records only from the additional section; a TSIG record placed in the answer or authority section survives and is signed again, causing encoding to recurse into itself with no termination condition. The decoder detects such a misplaced TSIG and logs a "misplaced or corrupt TSIG" warning, but does not reject the message as RFC 8945 §5.2 requires, leaving the malformed record in place. The bug triggers only when the TSIG carries an empty MAC and only in code that re-encodes a decoded message, such as a DNS forwarder or proxy; each recursive cycle re-encodes the whole message, so under 100 bytes on the wire can exhaust available memory and crash the process. Note that two other recent CVEs sometimes associated with Net::DNS — an eval-injection flaw in EDNS EXTENDED-ERROR parsing and a stack-exhaustion DoS via chained compression pointers — were already resolved in the prior 1.56 release, not in 1.57.

curl 8.22.0 (released September 2, 2026) addressed nine security issues in curl/libcurl and one in the wcurl wrapper script. The most notable is CVE-2026-19931 (Medium), a Negotiate-authentication flaw allowing connection reuse across different users. The remaining issues are rated Low, including CVE-2026-13608 (OpenLDAP SASL authentication bypass via MITM), CVE-2026-18924 (HTTP/2 server push use-after-free), and two OpenSSL-related flaws: CVE-2026-80229 (provider use-after-free) and CVE-2026-80230 (public-key pinning bypass). Also fixed: CVE-2026-80231 (native CA store connection reuse), CVE-2026-80255 (secure cookie attribute bypass), CVE-2026-82208 (wolfSSL CA-cache overriding verification callback), and CVE-2026-82209 (cookie leakage across Public Suffix List boundaries). The wcurl script separately received CVE-2026-80256, a backslash-handling bypass. No active exploitation has been reported for any of these issues.

libde265 1.1.2 (released September 2, 2026) is a security and bugfix release addressing two medium-severity memory-safety issues, both reported before CVE numbers were assigned. The first, GHSA-xp3h-6f5r-8cxp, is a heap use-after-free and double-free in multi-threaded (WPP) decoding: a crafted stream that repeated or rewound its slice_segment_address within a picture caused already-finished CTB rows to be re-run, breaking the ordered CABAC context handoff and freeing the shared context table twice. It is fixed by rejecting out-of-order slice segments and resetting WPP row progress per segment. The second, GHSA-mm7m-v26f-wf8x, is a heap use-after-free after de265_reset(), where a dangling previous-slice-header pointer was read by a dependent slice pushed after the reset. The release also adds hardening not tied to a CVE: rejection of NAL units shorter than the required header (avoiding a NULL-destination memcpy), a corrected SEI payload-size overflow guard that previously never triggered, and atomic per-CTB progress tracking to eliminate data races detected under multi-threaded decoding.

libxml2 2.15.4 addresses a single security issue, CVE-2026-86138, an integer overflow leading to a heap-based buffer overflow in the xmlDictAddQString function in dict.c. This function is part of libxml2's internal string-dictionary subsystem, used to intern qualified (prefix:local) names encountered while parsing XML. Because buffer-size calculations for these interned strings were not properly checked for overflow, a specially crafted XML document could trigger an undersized allocation followed by an out-of-bounds heap write, resulting in memory corruption. Depending on heap layout, exploitation could cause a crash (denial of service) or potentially more serious impact. The issue affects all libxml2 versions prior to 2.15.4 and is fixed by adding proper integer-overflow checks and boundary validation before the buffer is allocated. No other CVEs are associated with this specific point release, making it a narrowly scoped security patch rather than a broader maintenance release.

7-Zip 26.03 (released September 2026) addresses one named security issue, CVE-2026-58052, a Mark-of-the-Web (MotW) preservation failure. The flaw is in the guard that suppresses an archive-supplied Zone.Identifier stream during extraction: it matched only the exact literal name, so a crafted archive (e.g., RAR5) could bypass it and strip the Internet-zone marker from extracted files. Without MotW, Windows SmartScreen and Office Protected View do not warn the user, making this an effective technique for delivering phishing payloads that open without any security prompt. The issue is rated Medium severity, requiring only that a user extract the malicious archive, with no elevated privileges needed. It affects Windows only, since MotW relies on NTFS alternate data streams. 7-Zip's release notes list only this one CVE for 26.03, alongside unspecified general bug and vulnerability fixes. This follows a series of memory-safety CVEs patched in the prior 26.01 and 26.02 releases, none of which are re-listed as being addressed again in 26.03.

libpcap 1.10.7 (released September 5, 2026) fixes seven vulnerabilities, all Medium severity, in the BPF filter interpreter and remote-capture (rpcap) code. CVE-2026-0799 allows an unvalidated scratch-memory register index in a crafted filter to read/write process memory far outside bounds. CVE-2026-31912 stems from the interpreter failing to detect the end of a filter program or invalid jump targets, risking out-of-bounds reads. CVE-2026-31911 lets a crafted filter with an invalid opcode trigger an abort(), crashing the process. CVE-2026-6244 is a divide-by-zero in the div/mod ALU instructions, and CVE-2026-6554 involves mishandling of the jump offset in the "ja L" instruction, both crash-capable. On the remote-capture side, CVE-2026-18313 lets rpcapd allocate up to 65,536 bytes per UPDATEFILTER request without adequate limits, enabling resource exhaustion, while CVE-2026-18238 is a memory-safety flaw in the rpcap client's handling of PACKET messages from a remote daemon. All issues are triggered via crafted filter programs or rpcap messages, primarily causing denial of service or out-of-bounds memory access rather than confirmed code execution.

GStreamer 1.28.7 (released September 7, 2026) addresses five security advisories. GStreamer-SA-2026-0082 (CVE-2026-85150) is a NULL pointer dereference when parsing the RTSP Authorization header, allowing a crash via malformed requests. GStreamer-SA-2026-0081 covers out-of-bounds reads and writes in the FFmpeg-based audio encoder/decoder when handling excessive channel counts, risking memory corruption from crafted streams. GStreamer-SA-2026-0080 is a credential-leakage issue in souphttpsrc, where authentication credentials could be forwarded across cross-origin HTTP redirects, exposing them to untrusted servers. GStreamer-SA-2026-0079 fixes an integer overflow and out-of-bounds read in the MOV/MP4 demuxer's closed-caption parser, triggerable by a malformed file. GStreamer-SA-2026-0074 addresses unbounded source-table growth in RTP session management, where packets from many distinct sources could exhaust memory (mitigated by limiting tracked remote sources in rtprecv). Only CVE-2026-85150 currently has an assigned CVE ID; the remaining advisories are tracked via GStreamer's internal SA numbering pending CVE assignment.

libfuse 3.18.3 (September 9, 2026) addresses a cluster of security issues, none of which have CVE identifiers assigned. The most significant change disables fuse_session_custom_io() by default (requiring an explicit -Denable-custom-io=true build flag), since a custom I/O peer need not be the kernel and could forge requests that libfuse parses without bounds checks, crashing or corrupting the filesystem process. The remaining fixes harden fusermount3 and its mount-handling library against symlink races and privilege-escalation paths: the mountpoint is now resolved once via an O_PATH|O_NOFOLLOW descriptor to prevent symlink-swap redirection, the auto-unmount probe runs as the calling user instead of with elevated privileges, and unmount/mount argument vectors are terminated with -- so a caller-controlled fsname can no longer inject positional operands into a setuid-root mount(8)/umount(8) call. Additional fixes add UMOUNT_NOFOLLOW on relevant unmount paths, check an unchecked fstat() return value, fix an out-of-bounds read at index -1 in get_mnt_opts(), and fix a pointer underflow when trimming fuse.conf lines. A non-security correctness fix also relays KILLPRIV_V2 suid/sgid-clearing flags to filesystems via a new fuse_file_info::kill_suidgid field, which requires filesystems and the runtime library both be built against 3.18.3.

libheif 1.23.4 (released September 6, 2026) is a security and bugfix release; three of the fixed issues are rated High severity, and CVE numbers had not yet been assigned at release time. The detailed advisory, GHSA-vg7w-rp4 9-4fc2, addresses a missing enforcement of the max_items security limit on the child boxes of the iinf box. A crafted HEIF file could declare an unbounded number of items, causing the per-item iref reference scan to run in quadratic time — an algorithmic-complexity denial-of-service. The fix checks the limit before parsing child boxes, bounds the declared item count by the remaining input size, and reports a short read as an error instead of silently returning fewer items than declared. This release continues an active run of libheif security patches: 1.23.3 fixed a Critical heap buffer overflow in the uncompressed (unci) decoder and a High-severity decoder deadlock; 1.23.2 fixed two Critical issues, including one with a confirmed working code-execution exploit via derived-item (iden/auxl) pixel-plane handling. Users running any 1.23.x release prior to 1.23.4 are strongly encouraged to upgrade. ~

GIMP 3.2.6 is a security-focused maintenance release that patches 28 vulnerabilities, all located in the application's file-format import/export plug-ins rather than its core. Most are memory-safety issues in native parsing code — integer overflows leading to undersized buffer allocations, and subsequent heap or stack buffer overflows — affecting loaders for PSD, TIFF, SGI, and APNG images. Additional fixes address an unsigned-integer underflow enabling arbitrary writes in the PSD plug-in, a heap overflow in the Seattle Film Works loader, an overflow-driven heap corruption in FITS/cfitsio pixel-row handling, a signed-integer overflow causing denial of service in FLI file processing, and an out-of-bounds read in the ICNS plug-in that can leak heap memory as pixel data. All issues require a user to open a maliciously crafted image file; none are remotely exploitable without user interaction, and none affect GIMP's core engine, GEGL, or its scripting interfaces. Users who process files from untrusted sources should update promptly.

In GLib 2.90.0 a Heap Overflow on GLib through _xdg_mime_magic_parse_magic_line() in gio/xdgmime/xdgmimemagic.c via Incorrect Byte-Swap Pointer Arithmetic on MIME magic content in user- writable XDG data location was fixed

OpenSSL 4.0.2 is a security patch release fixing eleven CVEs, the most severe rated Moderate, with no remote code execution paths. Three Moderate issues were addressed: a QUIC server double-free on malformed INITIAL packets (CVE-2026-18798), a CMS heap buffer overflow during key unwrapping (CVE-2026-63072), and an invalid pointer dereference in CMP protection verification (CVE-2026-63076). The remaining Low-severity fixes cover an AEAD tag-verification bypass on empty ciphertexts (CVE-2026-75803), a NULL dereference in raw public key handling (CVE-2026-14457), a DTLS memory-amplification denial of service (CVE-2026-54874), a CMP format-string crash (CVE-2026-63073), unbounded CMP extraCerts cache growth (CVE-2026-63074), QUIC ACK-only packet memory retention (CVE-2026-63075), unbounded QUIC channel queue growth (CVE-2026-14456), and a client-side memory leak in OCSP response checking (CVE-2026-54876).

Expat 2.8.4 is a security release addressing four vulnerabilities, all denial-of-service risks rather than memory-corruption or code-execution bugs. The most notable, CVE-2026-66046 and CVE-2026-76641 (CVSS 7.5), fixed quadratic-runtime behavior in attribute isCdata lookups, where a moderately sized crafted document with many attributes could cause disproportionate CPU consumption; the fix replaces a linear scan with a hash-table lookup. CVE-2026-76957 hardens custom encoding callbacks against unsafe parser re-entry, related to a family of earlier re-entrancy issues fixed in Expat 2.8.2. CVE-2026-76956 (CVSS 5.9) corrected inverted return-value handling for getentropy(), which could cause weak entropy to be used for internal hash seeding in configurations relying on it, enabling hash-flooding denial-of-service attacks. None of the four issues allow remote code execution; all are availability-impacting.

PCRE2 10.48 fixes seven vulnerabilities, primarily memory-safety issues reachable through untrusted patterns or subject strings. GHSA-2p8c-ff85-vh9x fixed an out-of-bounds read when a pattern JIT-compiled for one match mode was matched in another mode against invalid UTF input. GHSA-q8g2-wprr-34m9 addressed an out-of-bounds heap write in pcre2_convert() on 32-bit platforms, and CVE-2026-86145 (GHSA-3r4p-g7gg-ppmf) fixed an out-of-bounds write in DFA matching under a heap limit, along with related integer overflows causing workspace under-allocation. GHSA-fmgr-6ggq-9859 added bounds checks for integer overflows during pattern compilation on 32-bit CPUs that could cause under-allocation and out-of-bounds writes. GHSA-9qww-pwc4-77qq fixed two out-of-bounds reads when scanning backwards through invalid UTF data. A further fix (issue #937) resolved a memory leak and invalid free in pcre2_jit_match() when reusing match data from PCRE2_COPY_MATCHED_SUBJECT. Finally, GHSA-q7rw-r7qq-2hx6 (low severity) fixed exposure of two uninitialized bytes via pcre2_serialize_encode().

XZ Utils 5.8.4 fixes a single memory-safety vulnerability, tracked as GHSA-5qpq-xqfv-j9pg (CVE pending at release), affecting all XZ Utils versions since 5.0.0. The bug occurs in lzma_alone_decoder(), lzma_lzip_decoder(), lzma_auto_decoder() (for .lzma/.lz files), and lzma_microlzma_decoder(). When a decoder is reinitialized and reused on the same lzma_stream object, and an intervening decode attempt fails with LZMA_MEM_ERROR, a subsequent reinitialization and decode using the same dictionary size can trigger an invalid memory write, at minimum causing a crash. Decoders for the standard .xz format and raw streams are not affected — only the legacy .lzma, .lz, and MicroLZMA code paths. The fix has also been backported to the older v5.2, v5.4, and v5.6 branches, though no new point releases will be made from them. The release additionally bundles two non-security correctness fixes: lzma_stream_buffer_decode() returning the wrong error code for truncated input, and a performance issue in lzma_index_cat() affecting concatenated .xz files. This issue is unrelated to the 2024 XZ Utils backdoor (CVE-2024-3094).

glib-networking's most notable recent fix (2.90.0) addresses CVE-2026-10028, an infinite loop in the GnuTLS backend's certificate chain verification. When building the in-memory certificate chain, issuer links between peer-supplied certificates are established via gnutls_x509_crt_check_issuer() with no cycle detection; a maliciously crafted chain with circular issuer relationships causes unbounded traversal during verification, consuming excessive CPU and resulting in denial of service for the affected process. Also relevant are two OpenSSL-backend issues, CVE-2025-60018 and CVE-2025-60019: the backend failed to check the return value of BIO_write(), causing an out-of-bounds read, and failed to check memory-allocation return values elsewhere, risking a write to invalid memory under an out-of-memory condition. Since most distributions build glib-networking with the GnuTLS backend only, these OpenSSL-specific issues affect a narrower set of deployments that explicitly enable that backend.

Firefox ESR 153.3, released September 15, 2026, addresses 63 security vulnerabilities across three severity tiers. Mozilla notes it has changed its disclosure practice and now issues a separate CVE for every internally found memory-safety bug rather than bundling them, which accounts for the unusually large count. Seventeen issues are rated high impact, including a cluster of eight related privilege-escalation flaws from incorrect boundary conditions in the Graphics: CanvasWebGL component (CVE-2026-92006 through CVE-2026-92013), a use-after-free in Web Codecs (CVE-2026-92005), sandbox escapes in Graphics and DOM: Core & HTML (CVE-2026-92035, CVE-2026-92018), and several further use-after-free bugs spanning the HTML Parser, XML, SVG, DOM Navigation, Networking, and DOM Streams components. About nineteen moderate-impact issues were fixed, largely use-after-free, privilege-escalation, and sandbox-escape bugs in Graphics, WebRTC, Win32 widget code, DevTools, and Enterprise Policies — notably CVE-2026-92054, a Memory-component privilege escalation reported by a researcher at OpenAI. The remaining seventeen issues are rated low impact, mostly sandbox-escape bugs in Win32 widget code, information-disclosure and spoofing issues in Networking and DOM Navigation, and denial-of-service bugs in SVG and Security components. Across the advisory, Graphics-related code (especially CanvasWebGL and Win32 widget handling) is the most heavily represented area, and most high-severity issues were discovered internally by Mozilla rather than external researchers.

Epiphany 51.0 fixes three security issues with assigned CVEs, plus related hardening. CVE-2026-18487 allowed address-bar host spoofing: a crafted URL like https://trusted.com:80@attacker.com/ displayed the trusted host while actually navigating to the attacker's site, enabling convincing phishing pages (Medium severity, requires a user click). Two more severe issues were fixed in the 51.rc pre-release and carried into 51.0. CVE-2026-77682 was a JavaScript code-injection flaw in form autofill, caused by building a CSS selector from an untrusted element id without sanitizing it, allowing a malicious page to run arbitrary JS (High severity). CVE-2026-77679 was a Zip Slip path-traversal bug in WebExtension (.xpi) extraction, where archive entries containing ../ sequences could overwrite arbitrary user files such as ~/.bashrc or SSH authorized keys, leading to persistent code execution. Additional fixes addressed a data: URI icon-handling code-injection issue and an XSS/HTML-injection flaw in the browser's error page, both hardening against untrusted content being trusted or executed.

Gvfs 1.62.0 fixes CVE-2026-88924, a privilege-escalation flaw in the admin backend: gvfsd-admin changed ownership of a private D-Bus socket via a link-following chown() on a path in a user-controlled directory, letting a local attacker race the operation with a symlink to a root-owned file (such as /etc/pam.d/su) and gain root. The fix sets socket ownership before creation, closing the race window. The preceding 1.61.90 release, bundled into 1.62.0, hardened input validation across the AFP, DAV, FTP, MTP, and SFTP backends — addressing unchecked server-supplied lengths in read paths that could otherwise corrupt heap memory, crash daemons, or leak memory contents (matching the pattern of several CVEs reported against these backends), and fixed related crashes in the MTP, OneDrive, and SMB backends. It also added clearing of password strings from memory before freeing, reducing exposure of credentials in memory dumps. Earlier still, 1.61.1 fixed a DAV redirect-handling bug that could allow an HTTPS-to-HTTP downgrade and credential leakage when following a malicious server's redirect.

Firefox and Firefox ESR 140.16 address 26 security issues disclosed in MFSA 2026-92, most rated High impact. The majority are memory-safety flaws — use-after-free bugs in the JavaScript JIT engine (CVE-2026-92021), Web Codecs (CVE-2026-92005), accessibili ty APIs (CVE-2026-92016), and several DOM subsystems (HTML Parser, XML, SVG, Navigation, Networking, Streams — CVE-2026-92 022 through CVE-2026-92 029). A cluster of boundary-condition bugs in WebGL/Graphics (CVE-2026-92006–92014, 92020) could enable privilege escalation, and a DOM sandbox escape (CVE-2026-92018) and WebExtensio ns privilege escalation (CVE-2026-92015) were also fixed. Two moderate-severity issues covered information disclosure and a mitigation bypass.

stunnel 5.81 (2026-09-16, urgency: High) addresses three security issues, none of which have been assigned CVE identifiers. First, it fixes truncation and out-of-bounds reads that occurred when inheriting binary session ticket keys containing embedded null bytes. Second, it prevents OCSP stapling response failures from terminating the running daemon, closing off a remotely triggerable denial-of-service condition. Third, it rejects excessively nested configuration file include directives instead of allowing them to recurse and exhaust the process stack, which could otherwise be abused for a stack-exhaustion crash. The release also includes several related bugfixes: a crash when parsing empty ASCII PSK secrets, a memory leak following DTLS listener poll errors and timeouts, and memory leaks during NTLM HTTP proxy negotiation. Additionally, early startup logging was fixed to no longer occur before thread-lock initialization, removing a potential race condition at process startup.

BIND 9.20.29 (2026-09-16) addresses 14 vulnerabilities. Five allow denial of service via crashes, including CVE-2026-77692, an unauthenticated crash triggerable over DNS-over-HTTPS with a malformed SIG(0) request, and CVE-2026-76163, triggered by a single TKEY query. Others crash validating resolvers via crafted or cached responses: CVE-2026-19667, CVE-2026-19666, CVE-2026-80274, and CVE-2026-19662. Four issues enable resource exhaustion via SVCB/HTTPS alias chains, oversized key-tag sets, or repeated SOA/CNAME/DNAME records (CVE-2026-81563, CVE-2026-81736, CVE-2026-19668, CVE-2026-75029). The remaining four concern data integrity: forged NXDOMAIN or unsigned-delegation acceptance (CVE-2026-19941, CVE-2026-77119), premature serving of unauthenticated IXFR zone data (CVE-2026-19033), and out-of-zone delegation answers from malformed zones (CVE-2026-78301). No exploits are known in the wild, and no workarounds exist for any of the 14.

Exim 4.100.1 is a security-only release fixing four vulnerabilities. Two involve the PROXY protocol: an out-of-bounds read while parsing v1 headers (GCVE-25-2026-09-50-1), and a v2 header parsing bug where an uninitialized length field could leak memory contents to an attacker, though this requires a buggy or compromised proxy (GCVE-25-2026-09-55-1). A third issue is a use-after-free in the GnuTLS-linked build, triggered when a client closes the connection early during TLS session startup (GCVE-25-2026-09-51-1); since it needs no special configuration or authentication, this is likely the most broadly exploitable of the four. The fourth fix extends mitigations against SMTP smuggling attacks, building on the earlier fix for CVE-2023-51766, to close additional variants of message-injection sequences that the original patch did not fully cover (GCVE-25-2026-09-56-1). No CVSS scores have been published for these four identifiers, which use the newer GCVE numbering scheme rather than traditional CVE IDs.

Thunderbird 153.3.0esr addresses 66 security issues. Three are specific to Thunderbird's own mail handling: an ambiguous mail-header parsing flaw (CVE-2026-92 238), a buffer overrun in the IMAP client (CVE-2026-92 239), and an out-of-bounds read in the IMAP response parser (CVE-2026-92 240). The remaining 63 are shared Gecko-platform fixes matching those in Firefox ESR 140.16. Most severe are numerous use-after-free bugs across DOM subsystems (HTML Parser, XML, SVG, Navigation, Networking, Streams) and Web Codecs, along with privilege-escalation flaws in CanvasWebGL, WebExtensions, and WebRender, plus sandbox escapes in Graphics and DOM: Core & HTML (CVE-2026-92 005–92029). Additional moderate- and low-severity issues cover mitigation bypasses, information disclosure, race conditions, and further sandbox-escape and use-after-free bugs across Graphics, Networking, WebRTC, and Windows-specific widget code.

libheif 1.23.5 is a security release; one issue is rated high, so upgrading is recommended for all users. The high-severity fix (GHSA-v8qw-hwjv- 44hw) addresses memory exhaustion caused by a mismatch between a container's declared image size and the actual bitstream size, letting a small file trigger multi-gigabyte allocations. Three medium-severity issues were also fixed: a heap use-after-free/double-free when encoding TAI timestamps (GHSA-qwpf-5wf7- r996), memory amplification from JPEG 2000 palette boxes with zero columns (GHSA-9c75-9g8r- 4728), and a heap out-of-bounds read during alpha compositing of images with mixed-bit-depth color planes (GHSA-r7gr-2xm2- 23wf). Two low-severity issues round out the release: an unbounded JPEG 2000 reference-grid check in the OpenJPEG plugin (GHSA-q492-cfcm- 895h) and an out-of-bounds read reachable only through direct API misuse (GHSA-qfj5-c4pq- q998). CVE numbers were not yet assigned at release time.

libslirp-4.9.5 fixes two security vulnerabilities that can be triggered by a malicious guest in a virtual machine or container using libslirp for networking (for example, QEMU user-mode networking or slirp4netns). The more serious issue, href="https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-95508">CVE-2026-95508, is a heap-based buffer overflow in the DHCPv6 response builder. A guest-supplied DHCPv6 CLIENTID option can overflow the reply buffer with attacker-controlled data, resulting in a denial of service and potentially arbitrary code execution in the host process. This issue only occurs when the interface MTU has been configured below 1280 bytes; the default MTU is not affected. A similar flaw involving the TFTP blksize option is covered by the same CVE but may not be fixed in this release. The second issue, href="https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-95507">CVE-2026-95507, is an out-of-bounds read in the NC-SI emulation code when processing truncated OEM commands, which could crash the host process or disclose a small amount of host memory to the guest. After updating, restart any running QEMU or slirp4netns processes so that the new library is used.

ntfs-3g-2026.9.18 fixes eight security vulnerabilities that can be triggered by a corrupt or maliciously crafted NTFS filesystem. Most are heap buffer overflows or heap corruption problems in the code that parses NTFS metadata, which could allow an attacker to crash ntfs-3g or potentially execute arbitrary code. If ntfs-3g is installed setuid root so that unprivileged users can mount NTFS volumes, a local user could potentially use these flaws to gain root privileges. The issues affect index handling (GHSA-r6xj-6488-p8mv), runlist decoding (GHSA-mc3c-983p-wqm8), attribute lists (GHSA-wf3w-fjjg-x4w3), WSL extended attributes (GHSA-2c97-47cr-9xr8), the $LogFile restart area (GHSA-xrvx-6jrp-4q3x), and security descriptor processing (GHSA-x98j-3g35-f59x, GHSA-pc48-m7cx-qf72). A flaw in inode extent handling can also cause a denial of service (GHSA-jcjj-9262-6j6p). CVE identifiers have been requested but not yet assigned. Users should update before mounting untrusted NTFS media.

xdg-dbus-proxy-0.1.9 fixes a security vulnerability, CVE-2026-94422, that allows a malicious sandboxed application to bypass the D-Bus message filtering used by Flatpak and other sandboxing tools, resulting in a sandbox escape. The proxy did not verify that messages presented as replies were genuine. A sandboxed application could send a method call or signal carrying a reply serial number and have it treated as a reply to an earlier request, or send a forged reply to an unrelated peer that had never contacted it. Either technique could be used to send unauthorized messages to services outside the sandbox or to trick another application into acting on false data, which, depending on the application, could lead to arbitrary code execution as the user. The proxy now only accepts genuine method returns and errors as replies, and only when they are sent to the peer that made the original call. After updating, restart any running Flatpak applications, or log out and back in, so that the new proxy is used.

wireshark-4.6.9 fixes 19 security vulnerabilities that can be triggered by malformed packets captured from the network or by a crafted capture file. Most cause Wireshark or tshark to crash, loop indefinitely, or leak memory, resulting in a denial of service. They affect numerous protocol dissectors, including ZigBee ZCL, SCTP, SPDY, CSN.1, MBIM, IEEE 802.11, USB HID, X11, and TIFF, as well as several capture file parsers and the sharkd utility: CVE-2026-95386, CVE-2026-95387, CVE-2026-95388, CVE-2026-95389, CVE-2026-95390, CVE-2026-95391, CVE-2026-95392, CVE-2026-95393, CVE-2026-95394, CVE-2026-95395, CVE-2026-96415, CVE-2026-96416, CVE-2026-96417, CVE-2026-96418, CVE-2026-96420, CVE-2026-96421, CVE-2026-96422, and CVE-2026-96423. A more serious flaw in profile import, CVE-2026-96419, could allow arbitrary code execution if a user imports a malicious configuration profile. This release also fixes several memory corruption bugs that do not yet have CVE identifiers, including integer overflows in the LBMC, LoRaWAN, and SMB code reported as possible remote code execution vulnerabilities. Users should update and avoid opening untrusted capture files or profiles with older versions.

Parted-3.8 fixes two heap buffer overflows in the FAT filesystem resize code in libparted-fs-resize. CVE-2026-89088 is in duplicate_legacy_root_dir(). A crafted FAT12/16 root directory entry count makes it read more sectors than its buffer can hold. CVE-2026-89085 is in _init_fats() and fat_table_read(). Crafted FAT32 metadata can cause a zero-sized allocation that is then written past. Both require resizing a maliciously crafted FAT filesystem through the libparted-fs-resize API. The parted program itself does not resize filesystems and is not affected. The same release also protects against a 4 KiB buffer overflow in directory traversal on deeply nested FAT directories. It fixes a stack overflow in the parted "print" command for disks with more than 99 GPT partitions. It also adds checks that prevent size calculations from overflowing in 32-bit builds. These fixes are implemented as assertions, which are only compiled in when debugging support is enabled (the default). Building parted with --disable-debug removes this protection.

PHP-8.5.11 fixes an access control bypass in the FastCGI code used by PHP-FPM and php-cgi. CVE-2026-91768 occurs because the check for the listen.allowed_clients setting compared only the first 96 bits of a client's IPv6 address. As a result, an entry permitting a single IPv6 address also admitted every host in the same /96 range. An attacker on the same network segment could connect directly to the FastCGI socket and supply their own FastCGI parameters, which can be used to run arbitrary PHP code as the pool user. Upstream rates this issue as Medium (CVSS 6.5), but the potential for code execution makes it High in practice. Only installations where PHP-FPM listens on an IPv6 TCP socket and relies on listen.allowed_clients are affected. Unix socket and IPv4-only configurations are not affected. This release also adds range checking for numeric user and group IDs in the PHP-FPM configuration. Previously, out-of-range values were silently truncated. Upstream does not consider this a security issue.

FreeRDP-3.32.0 fixes 62 security vulnerabilities reported through GitHub security advisories. Upstream has not yet published the details or assigned CVE identifiers. The release notes say they will appear on the FreeRDP security advisories page in the coming weeks. The fixes cover protocol negotiation and RDSTLS authentication, the RD Gateway client, NTLM and Kerberos authentication, licensing, graphics and audio codecs, and the clipboard, smartcard, and other redirection channels. Many of them fix memory-safety bugs such as buffer overflows, integer underflows, out-of-bounds reads, and NULL pointer dereferences. Some of these can be triggered by a malicious RDP server when a client connects, or by a malicious client before it authenticates to a FreeRDP-based server. Previous releases with similar fixes included vulnerabilities rated Critical, leading to crashes or possible remote code execution. This release also changes the default target certificate policy of freerdp-proxy from accept-unless-denied to deny-unless-accepted. Users of the proxy may need to update its configuration file. All users should update to FreeRDP-3.32.0 or later.

Epiphany-51.1 fixes a vulnerability that allows a malicious website to read local files. CVE-2026-94291 occurs because Epiphany's internal view-source:, ephy-reader: (reader mode), and about: URI schemes could be embedded in an iframe by any web page. By framing a view-source: or reader mode view of a local file, a website could get the contents of files on the user's system. The fix registers these schemes as display-isolated, so ordinary web content can no longer load them. Upstream has not published a CVSS score, but because the attack only requires the victim to visit a malicious page, it should be considered at least Medium in severity (an estimated 6.5). This release also hardens several dialogs against Pango markup injection. These include bookmarks, saved passwords, the privacy report, site permissions, search engines, extensions, and synced tabs. Names and titles from websites or synchronized data could previously inject formatting into Epiphany's user interface.

The glibc-2.44 upstream fixes patch addresses six security vulnerabilities. The most serious is CVE-2026-19499 (High, CVSS 7.7), a buffer overflow in strfmon() and strfmon_l() when a right-justified monetary value is formatted into a buffer that is too small. The others are rated Medium. CVE-2026-19542 is a stack-based out-of-bounds write in tdelete() when it rebalances very large binary search trees. CVE-2026-18374 is a heap buffer overflow in fopen() when the mode string contains an empty ",ccs=" character set. CVE-2026-77117 and CVE-2026-80489 cause an infinite loop in iconv() when it converts crafted SHIFT_JISX0213 or EUC-JISX0213 text, which can hang applications that convert untrusted input. CVE-2026-8674 is an assertion failure in the DNS stub resolver. A very long search domain in /etc/resolv.conf, for example one supplied by a DHCP server, or in the LOCALDOMAIN environment variable makes every program that performs DNS lookups abort.

Python-3.14.8 fixes eight security vulnerabilities. The most serious is CVE-2026-19445 (Critical, CVSS 9.2), a use-after-free in the ssl module. A remote, unauthenticated TLS client can crash a server, or make it call through freed memory, if the server's sni_callback switches the connection to another SSLContext and the original context is no longer referenced. CVE-2026-19553 affects SSLContext.wrap_bio() and asyncio. When no server_hostname was passed, the TLS handshake completed without verifying the identity of the peer, even with check_hostname enabled. CVE-2026-19672 and CVE-2026-82049 are bypasses of the tarfile extraction filters. A crafted archive could create directories outside the destination directory, or use a hard link to a symbolic link to expose files outside it. CVE-2026-15310 is a denial of service in zipfile, where a small bzip2, LZMA, or Zstandard compressed member could expand into an unbounded memory allocation. CVE-2026-15806 caused urllib.request to send credentials stored for an HTTPS URL to the matching HTTP URL, exposing them in clear text. CVE-2026-17084 restricts the stringprep module and the IDNA codec to the Unicode codepoint attributes defined in RFC 3454. CVE-2026-93990 is fixed by updating the bundled copy of Expat to 2.8.5. It does not apply when Python is built with --with-system-expat, but the system Expat should then be version 2.8.5 or later. This release also fixes a crash when formatting a float or complex number with a precision close to INT_MAX.

Expat-2.8.5 fixes one security vulnerability, rated Critical by upstream (CVSS 9.8). CVE-2026-93990 occurs because Expat accepted a UTF-16 high surrogate that was not followed by a low surrogate. Malformed UTF-16 text could therefore pass through the parser and reach the application using Expat, which expects the parser to have validated it. The damage depends on how the application handles the malformed text. Expat now rejects such input with an invalid token error. Only documents encoded in UTF-16 are affected. This issue is similar to CVE-2022-25235. Upstream notes that Expat still has unfixed security issues, including CVE-2025-66382, a denial of service that affects all releases, and CVE-2026-66046. No fixes are available for these yet. See libexpat issue #1160 for the current status.

OpenSSL-4.0.3 fixes 14 security vulnerabilities. The most serious is CVE-2026-84782 (High). When a DTLS handshake message is retransmitted after a suspended write, OpenSSL can read past the message buffer. This can disclose heap memory to the peer or crash the process. CVE-2026-84783 (Moderate) is a use-after-free in the X.509 extension cache. A remote peer could crash a multi-threaded TLS client, or a multi-threaded server that requests client certificates. The remaining issues are rated Low. Five affect the QUIC implementation and allow denial of service through memory or CPU exhaustion, or traffic amplification: CVE-2026-35191, CVE-2026-42772, CVE-2026-54873, CVE-2026-75804, and CVE-2026-84784. Three are timing side channels that could lead to private key recovery for ECDSA on non-NIST curves and for SM2: CVE-2026-54872, CVE-2026-54875 (ARM64 and RISC-V only), and CVE-2026-77696. CVE-2026-72897 is an out-of-bounds access in TLS servers that call SSL_set_SSL_CTX() during a handshake, as servers selecting a context by server name do. CVE-2026-35189 causes excessive memory use when processing a crafted certificate. CVE-2026-75806 allows one unauthenticated datagram to terminate a DTLS 1.2 association. CVE-2026-75805 is a NULL pointer dereference in the CMP client. This release also fixes EVP_DecryptFinal() reporting success after an AES-SIV authentication failure, and an HTTPS to HTTP downgrade through a relative redirect in OSSL_HTTP_get().

PCRE2-10.49 is a security-only release that fixes one vulnerability, rated High by upstream (CVSS 7.6). CVE-2026-103111 is an out-of-bounds write during JIT-compiled matching. A regular expression that needs an unusually large amount of JIT stack, such as one with a very large number of capturing groups, could cause writes outside the memory of a growable JIT stack. This can crash the process or corrupt memory, and could lead to arbitrary code execution. An application is only affected if it matches patterns supplied by an attacker and provides its own growable JIT stack with pcre2_jit_stack_create() and pcre2_jit_stack_assign(). Applications that use the default machine stack, or do not use JIT matching, are not affected.

Util-linux-2.42.3 and 2.42.4 fix four security vulnerabilities. Three are in mount, and they apply when mount is installed setuid root and /etc/fstab has entries that ordinary users may mount. CVE-2026-76642 (High, CVSS 7.8) occurs because post-mount hooks, such as X-mount.owner and X-mount.mode, still ran after an external mount helper failed. This made privileged changes to the filesystem already at the mount point. CVE-2026-78410 is a race on the mount source path that lets a local attacker use symbolic links to redirect a privileged mount or ownership change to an arbitrary path. CVE-2026-78409 allows X-mount.subdir to follow symbolic links out of the mounted tree. CVE-2026-78408 is a file descriptor leak in nsenter and unshare. An additional fix for CVE-2024-28085 prevents wall and write from passing terminal escape sequences in the hostname of their banner. Out-of-bounds writes in more and pg, and an out-of-bounds read in the libblkid ISO9660 probe, are also fixed. Version 2.42.4 completes these fixes. It prevents a local user from replacing an fstab mount point with a symbolic link to redirect the mount, for example onto /etc. As a result, a symbolic link in the mount point path of an fstab entry no longer works for non-root users.

Firefox-153.4.0esr fixes 62 security vulnerabilities: 34 rated High, 20 Moderate, and 8 Low. Nearly half are use-after-free bugs in the DOM, WebAssembly, Canvas2D, XSLT, graphics, storage, and networking code, which a malicious web page could use to crash the browser or run arbitrary code. Fourteen are sandbox escapes, which allow a compromised content process to break out into the rest of the browser. One of these is in the GTK widget code used on Linux. The remaining issues include privilege escalation, uninitialized memory reads, information disclosure, same-origin policy and site isolation bypasses, spoofing, and denial of service. None is reported as exploited in the wild. See MFSA 2026-100 for details.

SpiderMonkey from Firefox-140.17.0esr fixes four security vulnerabilities, all rated High and all in the WebAssembly code of the JavaScript engine. CVE-2026-100769 and CVE-2026-100776 are use-after-free bugs. CVE-2026-100788 is the use of an invalid pointer. CVE-2026-100792 is a JIT miscompilation. Each could be used to crash the program using the engine, or possibly to run arbitrary code. To exploit these, an attacker must get the engine to run crafted WebAssembly code. In BLFS, SpiderMonkey is used by GJS, which normally runs locally installed code such as GNOME Shell and its extensions, so the exposure is lower than in a web browser. See MFSA 2026-99 for details.

Thunderbird-153.4.0esr fixes 63 security vulnerabilities, 34 of them rated High. Most are shared with Firefox and, according to Mozilla, cannot generally be exploited through email because scripting is disabled when reading mail. They are a risk when Thunderbird displays web content. See MFSA 2026-103 for the full list. CVE-2026-103500 (Low) is specific to Thunderbird. Opening an email of 2 GB or larger could cause a heap buffer overflow. Several of the shared issues are in code that Thunderbird uses to display HTML messages and fetch remote content, and do not obviously require scripting. These include a use-after-free in text and font layout (CVE-2026-100784) and in CSS parsing (CVE-2026-100815), memory errors in audio and video playback (CVE-2026-100756, CVE-2026-100783), and networking issues (CVE-2026-100767, CVE-2026-96869, CVE-2026-100822).

FreeRDP-3.32.1 fixes six security vulnerabilities reported through GitHub security advisories. No CVE identifiers have been assigned yet, and upstream has published details for only one of them so far. GHSA-9qqc-m43j-g4r2 (Moderate, CVSS 5.3) is a missing size check in the USB redirection channel. A malicious or compromised RDP server can use it to crash the client. The other five will appear on the FreeRDP security advisories page. The changes in this release add input validation in the graphics pipeline, including limits on surface dimensions and checks for integer overflow. They also tighten length checks across the redirection channels, validate H.264 decoding and camera redirection requests, and correct a bitmap size check that could never trigger. Most of these protect a client that connects to a malicious RDP server. This release also fixes a regression in FreeRDP-3.32.0 that broke copy and paste of larger data. See the release notes for details.

libpng-1.6.59 fixes one security vulnerability, rated Medium by upstream. CVE-2026-46675 is a use-after-free in png_read_end(). When decompression of a zTXt, iTXt, or iCCP chunk ended early, libpng left its zlib stream pointing into an input buffer that could later be freed. A subsequent call to png_read_end() then read from the freed memory. A crafted PNG file could use this to crash an application, or possibly to disclose or corrupt memory. Only applications that call png_read_end() before reading the image rows are affected. This release also prevents a double free of internal buffers after a memory allocation failure. Upstream describes this as hardening. It cannot be triggered by a PNG file alone.

libsoup-3.8.0 and the 3.7 development releases before it fix eleven security vulnerabilities. In WebSocket handling, CVE-2026-15709 allows unbounded memory use when a compressed message is inflated, CVE-2026-15711 allows oversized control frames, and CVE-2026-0716 is an out-of-bounds read. CVE-2026-66337 is an out-of-bounds read in multipart handling. Three issues expose credentials or private data. CVE-2026-66339 sends proxy credentials through a CONNECT tunnel to the destination server. CVE-2026-12547 could send cached proxy credentials to a different proxy. CVE-2026-15713 stores authenticated responses in shared caches. The others are a missing nonce check in Digest authentication (CVE-2026-3099), excessively long NTLM passwords (CVE-2026-0719), CRLF injection through the HTTP method (CVE-2026-3633), and an HTTP/2 body length error (CVE-2026-85534). The server code is also hardened against HTTP request smuggling.

CUPS-2.4.20 fixes thirteen security vulnerabilities, all rated Medium or Low. Most are missing input checks in the scheduler, cupsd. CVE-2026-55480 (Medium, 5.7) occurs because temporary PPD files were not opened in exclusive mode. CVE-2026-61702 (Medium, 5.3) is a missing check of the language value in a request. CVE-2026-87875 (Medium, 4.3) is incorrect handling of UTF-32 values in cupsUTF32toUTF8(). The Low rated issues with a CVE are unsanitized IPP attribute strings in the backend (CVE-2026-55453), user names not treated as case-sensitive for quotas and policies (CVE-2026-87876), unsanitized fax numbers (CVE-2026-55467), and an unsanitized recipient address passed to sendmail by the mailto notifier (CVE-2026-105326). Six further issues have no CVE yet. They include two scheduler crashes, job attributes that were not filtered from print requests, and a race in the scheduler's startup permission checks. See the CUPS security advisories page for details.

libheif-1.23.6 fixes eleven security vulnerabilities, four of them rated High by upstream. No CVE identifiers have been assigned yet. See the release notes for the full list. Three issues affect libheif as built in BLFS. GHSA-8p2c-9 wv4-rx4p (Medium) is a NULL pointer dereference when reading a crafted image sequence. GHSA-vv35-6 hxg-95x8 (Medium) allows the bit depth reported for an image to differ from that of the decoded data, which can mislead an application about buffer sizes. GHSA-hvwh-x pj6-ph5x (Low) is a use-after-free in heif-enc. A heap out-of-bounds read in colour conversion with libsharpyuv (GHSA-q7mw- 2fmm-5q94, High) is present, but the known way to trigger it from a crafted file needs decoders that BLFS does not build. The other High rated issues are memory and CPU exhaustion in the uncompressed codec and the OpenJPEG decoder plugin. They, and two issues in the FFmpeg decoder plugin, only apply if those components are enabled.

OpenSSH-10.6p1 fixes several security issues. No CVE identifiers have been assigned. See the release notes for details. In sshd, GSSAPI credentials are now stored only after authentication succeeds, and GSSAPI state is reset before each authentication attempt. Options set to "none" inside a Match block, such as AuthorizedPrincipalsFile, were treated as a file name and so were not disabled. The "restrict" keyword in authorized_keys now fully applies to tunnel forwarding. In the clients, a malicious server could direct a recursive sftp download to write outside the target directory. User names containing "$" or a backslash given on the ssh command line could inject shell commands through ProxyCommand or Match exec, and are now refused. ssh-keygen mishandled daylight saving time, so certificate expiry times could be wrong by one or two hours. For both ssh and sshd, part of the compression algorithm is disabled to prevent recovery of plaintext from other channels of a compressed connection, and decompressed data is now limited to the maximum packet size. Compression is less effective as a result.

Xorg-Server-21.1.25 fixes twelve security vulnerabilities. A program connected to the X server can use most of them to crash the server or run arbitrary code in it. Where the server runs as root, this allows a local user to gain root privileges. See the X.Org security advisory for details. Seven are heap buffer overflows or out-of-bounds writes, in GLX (CVE-2026-93517), XKB (CVE-2026-93518, CVE-2026-93520), XFixes (CVE-2026-93519), RandR (CVE-2026-93521), Glamor (CVE-2026-93522), and XInput2 (CVE-2026-93523). Three are use-after-free bugs, in the Present extension (CVE-2026-93515), XInput passive grabs (CVE-2026-93516), and gesture handling (CVE-2026-93536). The remaining two are in XKB: a double free (CVE-2026-88812) and an out-of-bounds read (CVE-2026-93524).

Xwayland-24.1.14 fixes twelve security vulnerabilities. An X11 program connected to Xwayland can use most of them to crash it or run arbitrary code in it. Xwayland runs with the privileges of the user, so this mainly allows a sandboxed or untrusted X11 program to escape its confinement. See the X.Org security advisory for details. Also see advisory sa-13.1-058.

7zip-26.04 fixes several security vulnerabilities. Upstream documentation is scanty: the release notes only say that "some bugs and vulnerabilities were fixed", and no CVE identifiers have been published. The description below is based on a comparison of the source code with the previous release. These issues are rated Medium. Most of the changes add missing checks to the code that reads archives and disk images. WIM handling now limits memory use, validates file names, and checks that resources do not overlap. NTFS image handling has new checks in decompression and attribute parsing. VHD image handling now checks that reads stay inside the file. ISO directory records and Zip64 offsets and sizes that are out of range are now rejected. An integer overflow that could bypass the memory limit in the multithreaded XZ decoder is also fixed. These problems can be triggered when a user opens or extracts a crafted archive or disk image. The likely results are a crash or excessive memory use, and memory corruption cannot be ruled out.

The GStreamer-1.28.8 stack fixes eleven security vulnerabilities. Only one has a CVE identifier. See the GStreamer security page for details. Four can lead to arbitrary code execution. CVE-2026-86476 is an out-of-bounds read and write when deserializing media metadata in gstreamer and gst-plugins-base. A heap buffer overflow in the RTP audio depayloaders (SA-2026-0088) can be triggered by a malicious RTSP server. A stack buffer overflow in the closed caption elements (SA-2026-0085) is triggered by oversized caption data. A crafted project file can make gst-editing-services create arbitrary elements (SA-2026-0090). The other seven are out-of-bounds reads, excessive memory use, and crashes. They affect the Matroska, ASF, and SVG decoders, the H.265 RTP depayloader, RTCP handling, the RTSP server, and caps parsing in the core library. A crafted media file or a malicious network stream can be used to crash an application or disclose memory. All components of the stack should be updated.

Mutt-2.4.3 fixes two security issues. No CVE identifiers have been assigned. The more serious one is a heap buffer overflow in the code that converts a message between character sets (commit 7752d93f). A crafted list of character sets containing an empty entry caused Mutt to write past the end of an allocated array, and the amount of data written is not limited. This could crash Mutt and possibly allow arbitrary code execution. It can only be triggered when the user reuses a crafted received message as the template for a new message with the resend-message function. Upstream recommends that all users apply this fix. The second issue caused Mutt to mark a message as having a good signature in the message index when the signature could not actually be verified (commit 4364e5b0). A forged message could therefore appear to be correctly signed.

Aspell 0.60.8.2 has three memory safety vulnerabilities, all reported by the AFINE Team and fixed upstream after the 0.60.8.2 release. The first, CVE-2026-75818, is in the prezip-bin program, which compresses and decompresses word lists. When it processed a malformed compressed word list, it noticed that the input was bad but kept advancing past the end of the string, causing an out-of-bounds memory access. The second, CVE-2026-75819, occurs because the offsets in the header of a compiled (read-only) dictionary were never checked against the size of the dictionary data. A crafted dictionary file could make Aspell read outside the memory-mapped file and crash, or possibly disclose memory contents. The third issue, CVE-2026-75820, is in the code that adds words to a personal dictionary. The word length is stored in a single byte, so a word longer than 255 characters had its length silently truncated, leading to memory corruption. Applications that let users add words from documents they are editing could trigger this. Words longer than 250 characters are now rejected. All three issues need specially crafted input and are most likely to cause a crash. Apply the patch at https://www.linuxfromscratch.org/patches/downloads/aspell/aspell-0.60.8.2-security_fixes-1.patch to correct the problems.

Expat 2.9.0 fixes two security vulnerabilities, neither of which can be triggered by a malicious XML document alone. The first, CVE-2026-102633, is an integer overflow in the internal expat_realloc() function. The check that guarded against overflow when adding header and padding space to an allocation size was only an assertion. Assertions are removed from release builds, which left the check out on 32-bit systems that request extremely large allocations. The check is now always performed. The second, CVE-2026-77214, is in XML_ParseBuffer(). If an application passed a length larger than the space remaining in the buffer obtained from XML_GetBuffer(), Expat read past the end of the heap buffer, which could cause a crash or expose memory contents. Such lengths are now rejected with an error. Other robustness fixes include handling a failed allocation in XML_ParserReset(). See the Changes file for details.

Vim 9.2.1178 and later fixes two code injection vulnerabilities in the scripts shipped with Vim. The more serious, GHSA-x2w5-pj55-7hpc, is in the R Markdown syntax file, which reads the language name of each fenced code block so it can load that language's highlighting. A crafted language name could get past the script's input cleanup and reach a function that invokes the shell. As a result, simply opening a malicious .Rmd or .qmd file with syntax highlighting enabled could run arbitrary commands as the user. The second, GHSA-4xgr-vqh2-xfx8, is in the Ruby omni-completion script, which passed text taken from the buffer to Ruby's eval() to work out a variable's class. If a user requested completion in a crafted Ruby file, arbitrary Ruby code could run. This only affects Vim built with Ruby support. Both issues were fixed in patches 9.2.1177 and 9.2.1178.< /p>

FreeType 2.15.0 fixes two security vulnerabilities. The first (CVE-2026-50811) is an out-of-bounds read in the TrueType variable font code, introduced in FreeType 2.14.0. The second (CVE-2026-95512) is a denial of service in the CID font loader that can be triggered by opening a specially crafted CID-keyed font. A proof-of-concept exploit is publicly available for CVE-2026-50811. The severity of these issues is Medium, and all users of FreeType should update to 2.15.0 as soon as possible.

FreeRDP 3.32.2 fixes 45 security vulnerabilities. The most serious (GHSA-jq25-337 4-4262) is an incomplete fix for an earlier certificate validation flaw, which allows a man-in-the-middle attacker to impersonate an RDP server without the user being warned. Other fixes address use-after-free conditions in USB redirection, the proxy, and the gateway code, a heap over-read during clipboard image conversion, and a large number of denial of service issues that allow a malicious server or gateway to crash or hang the client, or a malicious client to disrupt the shadow server or proxy. None of these issues have been assigned CVE numbers yet. See the release notes for the full list of advisories. Note that a heap buffer overflow in PNG conversion (CVE-2026-109256) remains unfixed in this release. The severity of these issues is High, and all users of FreeRDP should update to 3.32.2 as soon as possible.

Firefox 153.5.0esr fixes 60 security vulnerabilities, and Firefox 153.5.1esr fixes one more. Mozilla rates 28 of these issues as High, 26 as Moderate, and 6 as Low. Many of them can be exploited by visiting a specially crafted web page. Several of the High severity issues allow a compromised content process to escape the sandbox, through use-after-free conditions, incorrect boundary conditions, and uninitialized memory in the Networking and Graphics components (CVE-2026-109705, CVE-2026-109707, CVE-2026-109708, and CVE-2026-109712). An additional issue in the process sandboxing code can lead to information disclosure and privilege escalation (CVE-2026-109709). Other High severity issues are use-after-free conditions in many components, including IndexedDB, text and canvas rendering, WebGL, crash reporting, WebIDL bindings, XML, the DOM, SVG, audio and video, animations, streams, and the JIT compiler (CVE-2026-109706, CVE-2026-109710, CVE-2026-109711, CVE-2026-109713, CVE-2026-109717, CVE-2026-109718, CVE-2026-109719, CVE-2026-109724, CVE-2026-109725, CVE-2026-109726, CVE-2026-109727, CVE-2026-109728, CVE-2026-109729, and CVE-2026-109732). Further High severity issues are JIT miscompilations and incorrect boundary conditions in the JavaScript engine and WebAssembly (CVE-2026-109715, CVE-2026-109716, CVE-2026-109720, CVE-2026-109721, CVE-2026-109722, and CVE-2026-109733), and integer ov erflows and incorrect boundary conditions in text layout and graphics (CVE-2026-109723, CVE-2026-109730, and CVE-2026-109731). These are the types of flaws that can typically be used to execute arbitrary code. The Moderate severity issues include additional sandbox escapes (CVE-2026-109745 and CVE-2026-109757; CVE-2026-109740 only affects Windows), use-after-free conditions (CVE-2026-109738, CVE-2026-109741, CVE-2026-109752, and CVE-2026-109765), privilege esca lation (CVE-2026-109743 and CVE-2026-109756), information disclosure, including in the PDF viewer (CVE-2026-109742, CVE-2026-109751, and CVE-2026-109767), a site isolati on issue (CVE-2026-109759), memory corruption issues in layout, the editor, and SVG (CVE-2026-109736, CVE-2026-109753, CVE-2026-109754, and CVE-2026-109762), a flaw in file handling in the DOM (CVE-2026-109744), and a number of s ecurity mitigation bypasses in the DOM, networking, file handling, and enterprise policy code (CVE-2026-109734, CVE-2026-109737, CVE-2026-109760, CVE-2026-109763, CVE-2026-109764, CVE-2026-109766, CVE-2026-109782, and CVE-2026-109783). The Low severity issues are a spoofing issue in Web Serial (CVE-2026-109770), denial of service in WebRTC and printing (CVE-2026-109775 and CVE-2026-109781), a race condition in XPCOM (CVE-2026-109776), information disclosure in IndexedDB (CVE -2026-109777), and privilege escalation in WebExtensions (CVE-2026-10 9778). Firefox 153.5.1esr fixes a cryptographic issue in the code that manages security block-lists and allow-lists (CVE-2026-113470). See the Mozilla advisories (MFSA 2026-108 and MFSA 2026-112) for more details. The severity of these issues is High, and all users of Firefox should update to 153.5.1esr as soon as possible.

Thunderbird 153.5.0esr and 153.5.1esr fix 66 security vulnerabilities. Most of them are shared with Firefox, because Thunderbird uses the same browser engine. These include sandbox escapes, use-after-free conditions, and JIT miscompilations that can be exploited through HTML email or web content. See advisory sa-13.1-068 for details on the 61 shared issues. Five issues are specific to Thunderbird. The account password could be sent unencrypted during Exchange account setup (CVE-2026-113866). The POP3 and SMTP NTLM authentication code could disclose uninitialized memory and read out of bounds (CVE-2026-113868). A stanza injection issue in XMPP chat could allow a remote attacker to inject messages or commands (CVE-2026-113867). A privilege escalation issue was fixed in the Application Update component (CVE-2026-109704), and a denial of service issue was fixed in Exchange email support (CVE-2026-110249). See the Mozilla advisories (MFSA 2026-110 and MFSA 2026-115) for more details. The severity of these issues is High, and all users of Thunderbird should update to 153.5.1esr as soon as possible.

curl 8.23.0 fixes 21 security vulnerabilities. The most serious is a use-after-free in HTTP/2 uploads, which can be triggered by a malicious server that resets the stream during an upload. The curl developers have shown that this can be turned into remote code execution under specific conditions (CVE-2026-92392). This issue affects curl 8.12.0 and later. The remaining 20 issues are rated Low by the curl developers. Several of them can leak credentials: passwords can be exposed through CURLINFO_EFFECTIVE_URL, a malicious HTTP proxy can obtain the credentials meant for the origin server, and Negotiate (Kerberos) credentials can be sent to a different origin after a redirect or through connection reuse (CVE-2026-94266, CVE-2026-86414, CVE-2026-94265, CVE-2026-86413, and CVE-2026-87861). Connections could be reused with the wrong local interface or client certificate (CVE-2026-107929 and CVE-2026-86415), and SSH host verification could be bypassed when following a redirect to SFTP or SCP, or when a known-hosts callback misreports a mismatched key as missing (CVE-2026-86410 and CVE-2026-87865). Servers could also erase or corrupt the cookie jar and HSTS cache (CVE-2026-92386, CVE-2026-86412, CVE-2026-87862, and CVE-2026-87863), cause an infinite loop or a stack overflow (CVE-2026-92387 and CVE-2026-92391), mix up FTP wildcard downloads or TFTP transfers (CVE-2026-92388 and CVE-2026-92389), or bypass the no-clobber protection for files saved with -J (CVE-2026-92390). Two further issues only affect builds that use GnuTLS or wolfSSL (CVE-2026-107928 and CVE-2026-87866). See the curl security page for more details. The severity of these issues is High, and all users of curl should update to 8.23.0 as soon as possible.

libarchive 3.8.10 fixes several security vulnerabilities, none of which have been assigned CVE numbers. These include an out-of-bounds read in the RAR5 reader when processing symbolic link targets (PR #3600), a heap buffer overflow during filename character set conversion (PR #3528), use-after-free conditions when a seek fails or when reading multi-volume archives (PR #3394 and PR #3447), and a heap buffer overflow in the compress writer when a write fails (PR #3664). Other fixes address infinite loops in the XAR and ISO 9660 readers and excessive memory consumption in the RAR5 and ZIP readers, all of which can be triggered by specially crafted archives. The severity of these issues is Medium, and all users of libarchive should update to 3.8.10 as soon as possible.

polkit 128 fixes several security vulnerabilities in the authentication helper and the authorization daemon. A local user could cause a denial of service by sending an excessively long input to the setuid polkit-agent-helper-1 program (CVE-2026-4897), and the initial fix for that issue introduced a one-byte out-of-bounds read (CVE-2026-85498). In addition, temporary administrator authorizations cached with auth_admin_keep remained valid after the approving administrator was removed from the administrator group, allowing a non-administrator to continue performing privileged actions for a limited time. This release also fixes a use-after-free in the authentication agent's session handling and prevents unsanitized values from authorization requests from being written to the system log. The severity of these issues is Medium, and all users of polkit should update to 128 as soon as possible.

cifs-utils 7.9 fixes a mount option injection vulnerability in mount.cifs (CVE-2026-104715). The username and domain values read from a credentials file were added to the mount options without being validated, so a value containing commas could inject additional mount options into a mount performed by root. A local user who can modify a credentials file used by a privileged mount (for example, from /etc/fstab, autofs, or a systemd mount unit) can use this to mount a share with root-owned setuid files and gain root privileges. A proof-of-concept exploit is publicly available. This issue affects cifs-utils 4.2 through 7.8. The severity of this issue is High, and all users of cifs-utils should update to 7.9 as soon as possible.

Nmap 7.992 fixes several security vulnerabilities, none of which have been assigned CVE numbers. Most of them can be triggered by a malicious host that is being scanned. These include two use-after-free conditions in the massdns parallel DNS resolver, unbounded memory consumption and infinite loops in several NSE scripts and libraries (some of which could not be interrupted by the --script-timeout or --host-timeout options), and unverified redirects in the anyconnect and upnp libraries. The afp library used a hardcoded Diffie-Hellman private exponent, which allowed an attacker who captured network traffic to decrypt the credentials being sent, and the predictable random number seed used by NSE could reveal the ASLR base address of the Nmap process. In addition, Ncat in listen mode could terminate the shell that started it. See the Nmap changelog for more details. The severity of these issues is Medium, and all users of Nmap should update to 7.992 as soon as possible.

Updates to five X.Org client libraries fix 17 security vulnerabilities. Most of them can be triggered by a malicious or compromised X server, or by anything that can forge replies and events sent to an X client, and can result in crashes or the disclosure of memory contents in the client. The most serious are an out-of-bounds write in the XKB action parser in libX11 (CVE-2026-88806) and two heap buffer overflows in XGetDeviceControl() in libXi (CVE-2026-109089 and CVE-2026-109090), which could potentially be used to execute code in the client. libX11 1.8.14 also fixes out-of-bounds reads in the XIM attribute parser, the XIM trigger-key parser, and the byte-oriented codeset parser (CVE-2026-94283, CVE-2026-94284, and CVE-2026-94285). libXi 1.8.4 fixes seven out-of-bounds reads when parsing input device replies and events (CVE-2026-93541, CVE-2026-93542, CVE-2026-93543, CVE-2026-93544, CVE-2026-93545, CVE-2026-94281, and CVE-2026-94282). libXrender 0.9.13 fixes an out-of-bounds read when parsing XRenderQueryFormats replies (CVE-2026-88807). libXtst 1.2.6 fixes an out-of-bounds read and an infinite loop in RECORD reply handling (CVE-2026-94286 and CVE-2026-109088). libXpm 3.5.20 fixes a denial of service caused by an unsigned integer underflow when writing XPM files (CVE-2026-94287). See the X.Org advisory for more details. The severity of these issues is Medium, and all users of these libraries should update to libX11-1.8.14, libXi-1.8.4, libXpm-3.5.20, libXrender-0.9.13, and libXtst-1.2.6 as soon as possible.

libcupsfilters 2.1.2 fixes four security vulnerabilities that can be triggered by submitting a specially crafted print job. A PDF file with excessively large page dimensions could cause an out-of-bounds write in the PDF to raster filter (CVE-2025-64503), and a TIFF image with an unexpected color space or bit depth could cause a heap buffer overflow (CVE-2025-57812). Malformed PNG or JPEG images could abort the filter process (CVE-2026-64612), and a malformed printer device ID could cause an infinite loop (CVE-2026-64611). This release also fixes several crashes found during a security audit. The severity of these issues is Medium, and all users of libcupsfilters should update to 2.1.2 as soon as possible.

certifi 2026.10.19 removes the emSign root certificates from its bundled certificate store. Intermediate certificates issued under these roots were revoked after their private key was compromised, so the compromised key could be used to issue certificates that would be trusted by Python applications using certifi, allowing man-in-the-middle attacks (GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2). No CVE has been assigned to this issue. The severity of this issue is Critical, and all users of certifi should update to 2026.10.19 as soon as possible.

NSS 3.131.1 removes three eMudhra emSign root certificates (emSign Root CA - G3, emSign Root CA - C1, and emSign ECC Root CA - C3) from its built-in certificate store (Bug 2084101 and Bug 2083709). Intermediate certificates issued under these roots were revoked after their private key was compromised, so the compromised key could be used to issue certificates that would be trusted by applications using NSS, allowing man-in-the-middle attacks. No CVE has been assigned to this issue. Because the system certificate store created by make-ca is generated from the NSS certificate data, users must also run make-ca -g as the root user after updating NSS.
