The severity of this issue is High, and all users of NSS should update to 3.131.1 as soon as possible.

c-ares 1.34.9 fixes eleven security vulnerabilities, none of which have been assigned CVE numbers. When more than one DNS server was configured, c-ares could accept a DNS reply from a server other than the one that was queried, allowing a malicious server or an off-path attacker to inject forged answers into the cache and bypass DNS cookie protection ( GHSA-fqh5-3x7m-wp44). The remaining issues are use-after-free conditions, memory corruption, and a buffer overflow that can occur when lookups are cancelled, servers are changed, or channels are shut down from callbacks or other threads, as well as the disclosure of uninitialized memory when resolving numeric IPv6 addresses. See the release notes for the full list of advisories. The severity of these issues is Medium, and all users of c-ares should update to 1.34.9 as soon as possible.

PHP 8.5.12 fixes two critical vulnerabilities in the PHP core that allow unauthenticated remote code execution. When an out-of-memory condition occurred during request initialization, PHP could leave an incomplete request state behind that was later used during shutdown (CVE-2026-109618). In addition, a global state that pointed into request memory was not always cleared between requests, allowing a later request handled by the same worker process to trigger a use-after-free (CVE-2026-109619). Working exploits have been demonstrated over HTTP against PHP running under Apache with mod_php, and CVE-2026-109619 has also been exploited against PHP-FPM. There is no configuration workaround for either issue. This release also fixes many other memory safety issues, including several use-after-free conditions and heap buffer overflows in various extensions. The severity of these issues is Critical, and all users of PHP should update to 8.5.12 as soon as possible.

BIND 9.20.30 fixes four security vulnerabilities in the named server. The most serious is a memory corruption issue in GSS-TSIG handling, where concurrent messages signed with the same key could corrupt internal state and potentially allow remote code execution on servers that use GSS-TSIG for Kerberos-authenticated dynamic updates (CVE-2026-94300). A remote attacker could also send specially crafted messages with excessive name compression to cause excessive CPU and memory consumption (CVE-2026-19630), and named could crash when a redirect zone is used together with strict QNAME minimization (CVE-2026-96888) or when certain Response Policy Zone configurations receive specific query patterns (CVE-2026-97313). No workarounds are available for any of these issues. The severity of these issues is High, and all users of BIND should update to 9.20.30 as soon as possible.

brotli 1.2.1 fixes a critical vulnerability in the Brotli decoder (CVE-2026-111497). An unchecked return value allows a specially crafted compressed stream to write out of bounds and corrupt the decoder's internal state, which can be used to disclose memory contents, cause a denial of service, or execute arbitrary code. Any application that decompresses untrusted Brotli data is affected, including HTTP clients and servers that support Brotli content encoding and programs that load WOFF2 fonts. This issue affects brotli 1.0.3 through 1.2.0. The severity of this issue is Critical, and all users of brotli should update to 1.2.1 as soon as possible.

Node.js 26.12.1 fixes nine security vulnerabilities in Node.js itself. The most serious are in TLS certificate hostname verification, where non-canonical IP address strings (such as octal or hexadecimal notation) and hostnames containing fullwidth Unicode digits could be matched against certificates issued for a different host, allowing a server to be impersonated (CVE-2026-106069, CVE-2026-105483, and CVE-2026-106072). In addition, DNS resolution truncated hostnames containing NUL characters, allowing a different name to be resolved than the one that was checked against an allowlist (CVE-2026-105482), and an HTTP keep-alive client could accept a response that a server wrote to an idle connection before the request was sent (CVE-2026-105481). Other fixes address repeated random values from crypto.randomUUID() and crypto.randomInt() in startup snapshots and single executable applications (CVE-2026-106074), disclosure of data from the wrong file position in ZipFile (CVE-2026-106070), and Permission Model bypasses through wildcard paths and fs.realpathSync() (CVE-2026-106071 and CVE-2026-106073). The Node.js release also addresses a critical vulnerability in the Brotli decoder (CVE-2026-111497). Node.js as built in BLFS uses the system brotli library, so this issue is fixed by updating brotli to 1.2.1, which is required for this update. See advisory sa-13.1-082 for details. The severity of these issues is High, and all users of Node.js should update to 26.12.1 and brotli to 1.2.1 as soon as possible.

7-Zip 26.05 fixes several security vulnerabilities, none of which have been assigned CVE numbers yet. Upstream has not described these issues, but examination of the source code changes shows fixes for out-of-bounds reads in the NTFS and VDI disk image handlers when processing specially crafted files, along with substantial rewrites of the Z (Unix compress) and Shrink decoders and the Mach-O handler. Previous releases of 7-Zip have fixed similar issues in archive handlers that could lead to remote code execution when a crafted archive is opened. The severity of these issues is Medium, and all users of 7-Zip should update to 26.05 as soon as possible.

The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates have been compromised. An attacker with the private key of any of the compromised intermediate CAs could impersonate any website or service. For details, see https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/. In BLFS, we use a centralized set of CA certificates, provided by Mozilla. Mozilla has released a new CA bundle which fixes the issue. You should install this new set as soon as possible by running make-ca -g -f.

Vim 9.2.1201 fixes a code-injection vulnerability in the Rust cargo quickfix plugin. When a user ran :make in a Rust buffer inside a crafted directory tree, such as a cloned repository, a directory name containing a "|" character could execute arbitrary Ex commands, and therefore arbitrary shell commands, as the user running Vim. A CVE has been requested but not yet assigned. This update also adds shell escaping of file names in the gnat and cppcheck compiler plugins, and fixes several memory-safety bugs in Vim9 script handling. For more details, see GHSA-x2w5-pj55-7hpc.

GNU patch 2.8.1 fixes a path-traversal vulnerability that allowed a crafted patch to create files outside of the source tree. When reverse-applying a patch that deletes a file, patch recreated that file without checking whether its pathname was safe, so an attacker who convinces a user or an automated workflow to apply a malicious patch in reverse could write to any location the user has write access to. This update also fixes a null pointer dereference and an infinite loop that could be triggered by malformed patches, and a symbolic-link resolution error that could cause patch to modify the wrong file. If you use patch to apply patches from untrusted sources, update to patch-2.8.1 or later. For more details, see CVE-2026-115207.

Python 3.15.2 contains several security fixes that are not present in Python 3.14.8. The most significant is a race condition in the cleanup of tempfile.TemporaryDirectory: an attacker who can modify the directory tree while it is being removed can replace a directory with a symbolic link, causing files outside of the temporary directory to be deleted or to have their permissions changed with the privileges of the process performing the cleanup. Several issues in the tarfile module's extraction filters have also been fixed. When extracting a link fell back to extracting an archive member, the filter could be bypassed, and the tar filter did not reject link members that resolve to the destination directory itself. Additionally, http.cookiejar accepted cookies with a negative Version attribute without checking their domain against the request host, poplib did not reject control characters in POP3 commands, allowing command injection, and a buffer overflow could occur when resolving very long paths. The ssl module now also refuses certificate chains that contain compromised eMudhra intermediate CA keys. If you use Python to process untrusted tar archives, HTTP cookies, or POP3 connections, or run Python programs that use temporary directories on multi-user systems, update to Python 3.15.2 or later. For more details, see CVE-2026-12345.

Samba-4.25.1 fixes an access control bypass in the experimental vfs_ceph_rgw module, which was introduced in Samba-4.25.0. When a client opens an existing file using different letter case, the module fails to look up the file case-insensitively and treats the request as a file creation, skipping the access check. An authenticated user can use this to read or overwrite restricted files on shares that use vfs_ceph_rgw. This module requires Ceph libraries that are not part of BLFS, so BLFS installations are unlikely to be affected. Only Samba-4.25.0 is vulnerable. This update also fixes a crash in vfs_acl_xattr and a build failure on i686. CVE-2026-109411.

glib-networking-2.90.1 fixes five security vulnerabilities. Three of them can affect BLFS systems built with the default GnuTLS backend: a remote TLS peer can cause unbounded memory growth by sending many TLS 1.3 session tickets, or by sending application data during the handshake, leading to a denial of service; and the client session cache key was not updated after a certificate property changed, which could allow resuming a stale TLS session. A fourth issue only affects the optional OpenSSL backend, which failed to validate the certificate purpose, allowing an Extended Key Usage bypass. The fifth issue only affects macOS. CVE-2026-103963, CVE-2026-113624, CVE-2026-113623, CVE-2026-113622, CVE-2026-112963.

libslirp-4.9.6 fixes several security issues that can be triggered by a guest virtual machine or container using user-mode networking. The ICMP echo reply length was not updated to match the data actually received, which could leak the host's real IP address to the guest under some conditions. The TFTP server did not check the space available in the reply buffer, completing the fix for a heap buffer overflow that could be triggered when the host is configured with a small interface MTU. The TFTP server could also read before the start of a buffer when given an empty filename. In addition, packets with invalid ("martian") addresses are now rejected. CVE-2026-115449, CVE-2026-95508.

Firefox-153.6.0esr fixes 145 security vulnerabilities, 95 of which Mozilla rates as high impact, 44 as moderate, and 6 as low. Most of them are use-after-free errors, invalid pointer uses, and incorrect boundary conditions throughout the browser, including the DOM, Layout, SVG, XML, XSLT, CSS parsing, Graphics (Canvas2D, WebRender and WebGL), Audio/Video, WebRTC, Networking, and the JavaScript engine and its JIT compiler. These can lead to crashes and potentially to arbitrary code execution when a user visits a crafted web page. Several of the vulnerabilities allow a compromised content process to escape the sandbox (in the DOM: Navigation, Form Manager, DOM: Networking, Storage: Quota Manager, Print Preview, Graphics, CanvasWebGL, WebRender and Widget components), and others allow privilege escalation (in the Networking, Canvas2D, WebRTC: Networking, Toolkit and UI Events components). Other issues include same-origin policy bypasses in the DOM: Navigation, CSS and Address Bar components, a JIT miscompilation in the JavaScript engine and in WebAssembly, information disclosure through uninitialized memory in the Audio/Video, Canvas2D and Networking components, site isolation bypasses in the HTTP, Service Worker and Navigation code, a cryptographic issue in WebRTC networking, a spoofing issue, and race conditions in the IPC and accessibility code. One of the moderate vulnerabilities (in the DLL Services component) only affects Windows. If you use Firefox, you should update to firefox-153.6.0esr as soon as possible. Thunderbird-153.6.0esr fixes nine security vulnerabilities specific to Thunderbird, in addition to the vulnerabilities it shares with Firefox (see advisory sa-13.1-093). Displaying a crafted message could cause Thunderbird to load an attacker-chosen URL through an OpenPGP key attachment, and replying to a crafted message could include the content of other messages in the reply, disclosing them to the attacker. Calendar discovery, RSS feed subscriptions and Matrix chat sessions could be redirected to local files or network shares, and the restriction on remote UNC paths in mailbox: URLs could be bypassed. A request forgery issue was also fixed in the handling of news: links. In addition, an integer overflow in the libmime buffer handling could lead to heap corruption while processing a crafted message, and a use-after-free in S/MIME decryption could occur while the security device password prompt was displayed. If you use Thunderbird, you should update to thunderbird-153.6.0esr as soon as possible. libheif-1.23.7 fixes sixteen security vulnerabilities that can be triggered by processing a crafted HEIF or AVIF image. Fourteen of them are rated high by upstream. They include a heap buffer overflow when padding an image to an inconsistent size, a heap use-after-free when grid tiles are decoded in parallel (only in libheif-1.23.6), a use-after-free or double free caused by a stale handle in heif_context_encode_thumbnail(), an out-of-bounds read in the OpenH264 decoder plugin, and two ways to bypass the coded-size check in the AV1 decoding path. Many of the remaining issues allow a denial of service through excessive CPU usage (from derived images, large numbers of coded pictures, transformation or colr associations, samples that produce no output, many chunks and stsc entries, and cyclic Exif IFD pointers), and a deadlock can occur during parallel grid decoding. In addition, the gdk-pixbuf loader could crash on certain files, and the heif-dec and heif-info utilities mishandled some sample entries. If you use libheif, you should update to libheif-1.23.7 as soon as possible. libjpeg-turbo-3.2.1 fixes several security vulnerabilities. A division by zero could occur when loading a non-grayscale indexed-color PNG image with an unspecified pixel format, causing a crash. A buffer overrun could occur when partially decompressing a crafted 4:2:0 JPEG image using merged upsampling and very small crop regions, and the RGB565 color converter could overrun its buffers when decompressing multiple scanlines at once. On 32-bit systems, an integer overflow could lead to a buffer overrun when loading packed-pixel images with more than 2^31 components. A use-after-free could occur when the same undersized destination buffer was used for multiple simultaneous transform operations. The TurboJPEG API was also hardened against reuse after a failed header decompression, which could lead to undersized buffers, and against applying one-pass quantization or RGB565 conversion to 12-bit JPEG images, which could overrun a color index array. If you use libjpeg-turbo, you should update to libjpeg-turbo-3.2.1. CVE-2026-75466.

aspell 0.60.8.3 fixes four security vulnerabilities that can be triggered when processing crafted dictionary or word list files. CVE-2026-103658 is an integer overflow in String::reserve() that leads to a heap buffer overflow when loading a crafted compiled dictionary, which may allow arbitrary code execution. CVE-2026-75818 is a heap buffer overflow in prezip-bin when decompressing a crafted file, CVE-2026-75819 is an out-of-bounds read caused by unvalidated offsets in a compiled dictionary header, and CVE-2026-75820 is heap corruption caused by truncating the length of very long words in a personal word list. Several other memory safety problems in the handling of affix, character map, and phonetic data files were also fixed. Update to aspell-0.60.8.3 or later.

fribidi 1.0.18 fixes several security issues that were found by an automated scan. No CVEs have been assigned. The most serious is an out-of-bounds write in fribidi_remove_bidi_marks() when the position maps returned by one call are passed to a later call. Text consisting of many back-to-back isolates, or of deeply nested isolates containing brackets, could also take quadratic time to process, allowing a denial of service in any application that uses fribidi (for example, through Pango) to display untrusted text. Other fixes include an integer overflow in the run-pool allocation on 32-bit systems that could lead to a heap buffer overflow, crashes caused by unchecked memory allocations, an out-of-bounds read in the CapRTL decoder on platforms where char is unsigned, and stack buffer overflows in the fribidi and fribidi-caprtl2utf8 programs when producing UTF-8 output. This release also brings bidirectional text handling closer to the Unicode standard, which may change the output for unusual input. Update to fribidi-1.0.18 or later.

libslirp 4.9.7 fixes several security issues that can be triggered by a guest using user-mode networking (for example, QEMU's user networking or rootless Podman containers). No CVEs have been assigned. The most serious is an out-of-bounds heap read in icmp_forward_error() that could disclose memory from the host process to the guest in ICMP error messages. A guest could also crash the host process by corrupting the packet queue in if_output() when one connection generates a large amount of traffic, exhaust host memory by repeatedly sending IPv6 pings to the virtual gateway because of a memory leak, and add ARP or NDP entries for multicast addresses and for libslirp's own addresses. Update to libslirp-4.9.7 or later.

libarchive 3.8.11 fixes several security issues, most of which can be triggered by processing a crafted archive. No CVEs have been assigned. A malformed ISO 9660 image with Joliet extensions could cause unbounded recursion and a crash, a crafted RAR archive could cause excessive memory allocation for a stored symbolic link, and a crafted XAR archive could trigger an integer overflow that caused its table of contents to be processed twice. When skipping stored entries in a streamed ZIP archive, file contents could be mistaken for the end of the entry, causing libarchive to interpret the rest of the archive differently from other tools. A memory leak when parsing ISO 9660 Rock Ridge entries was also fixed. The XAR reader no longer cleans up the global libxml2 state, which could cause crashes or use-after-free errors in applications that also use libxml2 themselves. An integer overflow in wide string allocation that could lead to a heap buffer overflow on 32-bit systems, and a crash when an extended attribute changes while it is being read, were also fixed. In addition, bsdunzip no longer crashes when reading an archive from standard input. Update to libarchive-3.8.11 or later.
